summary: Admit the existing bounded MAX HTTPS URL button adapter through the reviewed runtime-support, Social API, worker and UI path.

impacts.evidence: The existing account and channel capability settings remain tenant-scoped and are required before MAX button publication.
The existing bounded button snapshot contains only user-visible labels and HTTPS URLs; no secrets or provider payloads are added.
Task 181 already added the provider-neutral Social API button shape; Task 182 changes only runtime admission metadata.
Existing social events remain ID/state-only and no event schema changes.
The existing SocialButton and SocialPublisher interfaces are reused without SDK changes.
The Task-181 immutable variant button column is reused; no migration is added.
The existing HTTPS-only URL validation and MAX adapter row/count bounds remain enforced before egress.
Existing publication capability, account setting, worker lease and receipt recovery gates remain mandatory.
Existing publication, audit and receipt lineage covers the admitted MAX side effect without copying raw provider payloads.
MAX's existing ambiguous upload/send handling remains non-retryable and receipt-safe.
Only the already admitted MAX POST /messages egress is reused; inbound webhooks remain closed in the application runtime.
Existing Social worker leases, timeout, rate-limit and failure telemetry cover button publications.
Removing the runtime capability or account setting immediately prevents new MAX button publications.
Existing MAX adapter button tests plus the runtime-support assertion cover the admission boundary.
